Why The Canopy

Not art that fills a room.
Art that becomes one.

The Canopy is PHAÖRA's defining work — the piece that every collector who sees it asks about first. It is not a decoration. It is not an accent. It is the room's reason.

At 96 inches wide and 380 pounds, it is scaled for the spaces that deserve it: double-height lobbies, grand foyers, estate galleries, penthouse atriums. In every space it has occupied, the room was remembered because of it.

I
Seven individually carved birds Each white quartz bird is a separate carving — not cast, not molded. Feather striations are cut by hand. No two birds are identical.
II
Atlantic rainforest driftwood The driftwood base was sourced from Brazil's Atlantic coast and treated to preserve its grain for generations. There is no substitute material.
III
Crystal botanical accents Flowers and foliage carved from citrine, amethyst, and labradorite are worked into the driftwood at the junction points — visible only on close inspection.
IV
40 years in one piece Fabiano has been carving for over four decades. The Canopy represents the accumulated precision of that practice — it is not the work of a young artist.

Origin

Minas Gerais, Brazil

The mountains of Minas Gerais produce some of the world's most extraordinary mineral formations — amethyst cathedrals, white quartz veins, tourmaline, and aquamarine fields that took tens of millions of years to form. PHAÖRA sources exclusively from this region, working directly with the mining families who know which formations are worthy of becoming art. Every stone in The Canopy was in the earth before any living person was born.
